findings.item: 1) surrender-end-empty-frame-still: the board fades to ~50% and is gone, then 0.6-1.0 s of only the ambient digits (later the 'לבית' header), then 'הפסד'. Same in practice and with Reduced Motion.
findings.rootCause:
This is not the native race any more. The results screen draws nothing visible during the whole native fade, and that comes from our own design.

Loop 7 assumed that pushing /results over /game keeps the final board whole under the results' fade. On Android this is false. In react-native-screens 4.26.2, pushing a non-translucent screen REMOVES every fragment under the new top in the same fragment transaction, and the removed fragment gets the exit tween. For 'fade' that is rns_fade_out: alpha 1 to 0 over a fixed 150 ms. After that the game view is detached. So the board always disappears within 150 ms, whatever the results show. Push instead of replace only removed the race where the views were deleted before the tween ran. That fade is the frame QA sees at ~50%.

During those 150 ms the incoming results route shows nothing:
(a) Its first render is ResultsLoading, which stays at opacity 0 (styles.unseen) for RESULTS_QUIET_MS = 300.
(b) The data arrives only after a passive effect, load(), and afterFrames(RESULTS_AFTER_FRAMES = 2). A practice game also flushes and reads SQLite. Only then does ResultsBody render, and that render is heavy: the hero AvatarArt SVG, the opponents' avatars, rating, best move, stats, awards and actions.
(c) When ResultsBody mounts, only the header row (the 'לבית' ghost button and the caption) has no entrance. Everything else starts at opacity 0:
- avatar: 'rise' at 0 ms, 420 ms
- title: 'drop' at +200 ms, 420 ms
- tags and the end line: +200 ms
- score and sections: +700 ms or later
- actions: +1900 ms
With Reduced Motion every part still starts at 0 and fades in over 200 ms after mount.

The screenshots follow exactly this order:
1. the board
2. a frame at ~50%
3. digits only (the opacity-0 loading view; ResultsBody not drawn yet)
4. 'לבית' only (ResultsBody mounted, the hero still at opacity 0)
5. avatar and 'הפסד'

A 150 ms tween that starts at the push cannot hide a screen that only gets content hundreds of ms later. QA's ~0.9 s with Reduced Motion shows that most of the gap is (b): getting ResultsBody committed and drawn. The loop-7 drop adds to that window. The game's onDisappear fires at the end of its exit tween (~150-200 ms), and dropWhenCovered then resets the stack. The whole GameScreen tree is unmounted and its views deleted, on both threads, at the moment the results load, render and draw their SVGs for the first time.

- The exact split of the 0.6-1.0 s between the load, the 2 frames, the ResultsBody render and mount, and the concurrent GameScreen teardown: MEDIUM-LOW. No logcat or trace exists for APK 13; the qa-shots folder has only PNGs.
findings.proposedFix:
Two parts. Both are needed.

1. The results must have their content in the first frame of the stack fade.
- Build the ResultsLoad before navigating. Online, loadOnlineResults(id, online) is synchronous. Practice: start loadPracticeResults when the end is confirmed, during the dialog exit and hold, and push when it resolves, with a ceiling.
- Hand it to the route, for example a handoff keyed by gameId like handGoCover, or an `initial` prop. ResultsScreen's first render is then ResultsBody: no ResultsLoading and no afterFrames(2).
- RESULTS_AFTER_FRAMES existed because 'the results replace the game in one commit'. Since loop 7 that is false: the game's views are deleted at the drop, not at the push. Update that comment and the stale one in results/[id].tsx.
- The push commit then carries the heavy render. The board simply stays a little longer, which is not an empty frame.

2. Nothing in the hero may start at opacity 0 when the screen comes in on the stack fade.
- The avatar, title, place tag and end line start at opacity 1 and keep only their movement: drop/slam translate or scale. Alternatively, drop the hero's own fade on the 'just played' path and let the native 150 ms fade be its fade.
- With Reduced Motion the hero is static at 1; the native fade is the 200 ms fade.
- The later sections can keep their rises.
- Update the motion.md §4.7 rows results.title.loss/win and flow.fade to match.

Also recommended: delay the drop of the covered game until the results have drawn, for example the first ResultsBody frame plus SWAP_FRAMES, or ~1 s. A dropWhenCovered option with a minimum delay after covered would do it. Then GameScreen's teardown does not run in the same frames as the results' first SVG draws. Keep the drop under RESULTS_WATCHDOG_MS (4 s), or make GameScreen's watchdog ignore an unfocused screen.

Alternative, if the content cannot be made ready: present the results as presentation 'containedTransparentModal'. ScreenStack then keeps the game attached as visibleBottom (lines 176-180, 273-278 skip it). Fade the game out in-app once the results report drawn, then drop it. More moving parts: a11y focus beneath, back handling, iOS. Not my first choice.

Do not try animation 'none' alone: rns_no_animation_20 removes the game after 20 ms, so it is only a cut if the results are already fully drawn.

Tests:
- A Jest test that ResultsScreen's first commit (with a handed-over load) already contains results-title.
- A test that the hero's animated opacity is 1 at mount, with motion on and with Reduced Motion.
- A test that app/game.tsx pushes with the load handed over.

Device check: screenrecord the surrender with a board-to-hero cross-fade, and look for no digits-only frame.

findings.item: 2) results-newgame-empty-frame-intermittent: Results 'משחק חדש' to search, 1 of 3 times 170-500 ms of digits plus only 'ביטול חיפוש'
findings.rootCause:
The same pattern as item 1, on the search screen.

Loop 6's push and drop does keep the results intact for the 150 ms rns_fade_out, and that part works. But the incoming search screen's content starts at opacity 0:
- SearchView wraps the whole column (header chip, title, timer, radar, range, seats) in useEnter(reduce). Its shared value starts at 0 and only ramps 0 to 1 over 240 ms once a passive useEffect has run and the UI runtime picks it up.
- The footer with 'ביטול חיפוש' sits outside that wrapper and is at opacity 1 from the first frame.

So the native fade cross-fades the results into the cancel button alone. Whether the column has started rising by the time the results are gone (~T+150 ms) depends on the JS thread right after the push commit. It is busy then with:
- startRanked creating the matchmaking client and connection in the same task
- leave(), which clears the store and fires refreshMe
- the results' dropWhenCovered reset at transitionEnd (~T+150-250 ms), which unmounts the heavy ResultsBody
- the first room messages

This explains the intermittency: in 2 of 3 runs the 240 ms ramp overlaps the native fade and reads as a cross-fade. In 1 of 3 it starts late, and QA sees 170-500 ms of only the button, exactly what newgame-2.png shows: frames 3-4 contain only 'ביטול חיפוש'.

findings.item: 3) back-during-go-opens-surrender: Android Back while GO! is shown (game already mounted under GoCover) opens the 'אתה בטוח שאתה רוצה להיכנע?' dialog
findings.rootCause:
GoCover blocks Back only during its first phase, 'cover', which lasts a single frame. The cleanup of that phase's effect removes the blocker when the phase becomes 'under'. That is the same commit in which GoCover first mounts its children: OnlineGame, then GameScreen. GameScreen registers its own hardwareBackPress listener in a mount effect.

RN's BackHandler calls listeners last-added first and stops at the first one that returns true. So from 'under' on, through 'under' (2 frames that are long while the game's first draw is paid) and the 240 ms 'fade', GameScreen's handler gets Back. It runs back.current(), and since view.status === 'running' (playing), not blocked and not selfOffline, it calls openConfirm(). The surrender dialog opens over GO!.

MatchScreen's own blocker (which returns true for every phase from 'found' on) is still mounted under /game until the drop, but it was registered earlier, so GameScreen's later listener wins. Expected behaviour, per spec §10 (01-SPEC.md:1240: after 'נמצאו' there is no cancel, and leaving counts as abandonment [D32]), GoCover's own comment ('Android's back does nothing meanwhile (as from found)') and loop 6's device check 4 ('Android back during GO! does nothing'): Back must do nothing until GO! is gone.

- src/screens/match/GoCover.tsx:51-61: case 'cover' adds BackHandler.addEventListener('hardwareBackPress', () => true), then afterFrames(1, () => setPhase('under')). The cleanup calls sub.remove().
- GoCover.tsx:62-63: case 'under' runs afterFrames(SWAP_FRAMES, () => setPhase('fade')) with no blocker. Lines 64-68: 'fade' (240 ms, Reduced Motion 200) with no blocker.
- GoCover.tsx:82-84: {phase === 'cover' ? null : children}. GameScreen first mounts in the 'under' commit, the same commit whose cleanup removed the blocker.
- src/screens/game/GameScreen.tsx (currently ~1373-1393, back.current in useLayoutEffect): else if (playing && !blocked && !selfOffline) openConfirm(). The useEffect(() => { BackHandler.addEventListener('hardwareBackPress', () => { back.current(); return true; }) }, []). Line 480: const playing = view.status === 'running'.
- node_modules/react-native/Libraries/Utilities/BackHandler.android.js (RN 0.86.3), lines 30-31: for (let i = _backPressSubscriptions.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) { if (_backPressSubscriptions[i]?.(event)) ... break }. Lines 90-91: push, so the last added runs first.
- src/screens/match/MatchScreen.tsx:263-270: the match screen's handler (registered earlier) loses to GameScreen's.
- src/screens/game/online/OnlineGame.tsx:78-85: if the game is not there yet (!hasGame) under the cover, its handler calls onLeave. Back would then even leave the room (an abandonment).

Timeline:
1. GO! drawn on the match screen (useDrawnAt: 2 frames).
2. goHoldMs passes.
3. onPlay: handGoCover(go), then router.push('/game') with the 'none' cut.
4. Covered 'cover', blocker ON, 1 frame.
5. 'under': blocker OFF. GameScreen mounts at UNDER_OPACITY 0.01 and adds its handler.
6. 2 frames, long while the game's first draw is paid. QA measured GO! to board at 1.24-1.37 s.
7. 'fade', 240 ms, then the board.
QA's press was 0.3-0.6 s before the board appeared, inside steps 5-7, so GameScreen's handler opened the dialog. Screenshot: qa-shots/fix8-RF8Y30L038L-backgo-1.png.

Confidence: HIGH.
findings.proposedFix:
Keep Back blocked for as long as GO! is on screen, in a way that wins over any handler the children register.

Safest: GoCover exposes a 'covering' flag through a small context or a ref, true from mount until its fade has ended (not until the RETIRE_MS 'done'). GameScreen's back.current returns early while it is true: handled, nothing opens. OnlineGame's pre-game handler does the same.

Simpler but more fragile: Covered adds a () => true blocker in the 'under' and 'fade' phases as well. Passive mount effects run child-first, so in the 'under' commit it would be registered after GameScreen's listener and win (LIFO). But if OnlineGame mounts GameScreen later (hasGame turning true after 'under'), GameScreen's listener is added after the blocker and wins again. That is why the context or ref gate is preferred.

Remove the gate when the fade completes (setTimeout of fade.duration in the 'fade' case, or the withTiming callback).

Tests:
- A Jest test with the real GoCover and a GameScreen stand-in that registers BackHandler like GameScreen: fire hardwareBackPress in 'under' and in 'fade'. Expect no confirm and the event consumed.
- After the fade, Back opens the confirm.
- Repeat with Reduced Motion.
findings.risks:
- If the gate never clears (a fade callback lost), Back would stay dead in the game. Clear it on a timer as well as on the animation's end.
- The match screen is dropped under /game within ≤600 ms, so do not rely on its blocker.
- GameScreen.tsx is being edited by other agents at the same time. Keep the change to the back.current line plus a context read.

findings.item: 1) surrender-end-empty-frame-still (ranked surrender 4/4, practice 'סיום אימון' 3/3, Reduced Motion too)
findings.rootCause:
Two things combine, and both are in the code, not a race.

(A) Native: on Android, pushing a screen still fades the covered one out. Loop 7 assumed the final board 'stays whole under the results' fade'. That is false on Android. On a push, ScreenStack.onUpdate uses the new top's FADE as an open animation, and setTweenAnimations gives the outgoing fragment rns_fade_out (1→0, fixed 150 ms). The same pass removes every wrapper below the top that is not a translucent visibleBottom (transaction.remove(game.fragment)). So push and replace look the same: the board is gone 150 ms after the transaction. Push only took away the extra Fabric-deletion race. The GO! handoff works for a different reason: it uses animation 'none' (rns_no_animation_20) and the new screen's first frame is an identical, opaque GO!.

(B) JS: the results draw nothing visible during that 150 ms, and very little for about 300 ms after it. RNS runs the transaction just after the Fabric mount batch that inserted the new screen (ScreenContainer.onScreenChanged → runOnUiQueueThread(performUpdates)). So the cross-fade is board → the results route's FIRST commit. That first commit is ResultsLoading with its content at opacity 0: `if (!result) return <ResultsLoading/>`, styles.unseen {opacity:0}, RESULTS_QUIET_MS 300. The model arrives only after load() + afterFrames(RESULTS_AFTER_FRAMES=2) (app/results/[id].tsx:45-53). For a practice, load() is also await live.flush() + repo() + getGame + loadEvents.
When ResultsBody mounts:
- the header ('לבית' + caption) has no entrance, so it appears at once. This is QA's ''לבית' in the second half'.
- the hero starts at opacity 0: avatar 'rise' from +0 over 420 ms; title/badge from +200 over 420 ms (slamAt 200, rewardMin 420); score +700; sections +850…; actions +1900.
So 'הפסד' is readable only about 300 ms after mount.

(C) Amplifier (likely, not measured): in that same window, dropWhenCovered fires on the game's transitionEnd (about 150 ms after the push). It resets the stack, so the whole GameScreen unmounts on the JS thread and its native views are deleted on the UI thread, while the results load, run their rAFs and do their first render. cap.sh's parallel screencaps add load as well: QA itself measured GO!→board at 2.6–3.0 s under heavy capture against 1.37 s under light capture.

Reduced Motion takes away the delays but not (A) or the mount latency. That is why QA still saw 0.9 s (1 sample): most of that gap is push → ResultsBody mount, not choreography.

Confidence:
- (A) and (B): high (library source + our code + the screenshots match frame by frame).
- The exact device milliseconds and the weight of (C): medium.

- T0: tap 'כן, להיכנע'. Dialog out 240 ms, onExited at about T0+260. Surrender sent; gameOver at about T0+RTT (50–200); showResults(id, 600).

Reduced Motion:
- P ≈ T0+250–300 (hold 200, dialog about 200). The fade is still 150 ms. All parts fade 200 ms from M with no delays.
- The code alone predicts about 0.1–0.3 s. QA's 0.9 s (n=1) therefore means M was late: the mount latency.

Practice vs bot: the hold is 0 and the push waits only for the dialog exit (P ≈ T0+260–300). load = flush + 3 SQLite awaits + resultsModel + 2 frames, so M−P ≈ 100–400 ms. QA measured 0.5–0.9 s.

The unguarded window runs from about 1 frame after the game route mounts until GO! is gone: 2 frames ('under') + the 240 ms GO!→board fade (200 ms with Reduced Motion) + however long the game's first draw keeps GO! up. QA saw it 0.3–0.6 s before the board appeared.

findings.item: 1) density-change-orphans-ranked-game: root cause (why the game is lost and then counted as a loss)
findings.rootCause: Three causes in a chain. (1) `wm density` (and the Display size and Font size settings) recreates MainActivity, because the manifest's configChanges do not list density, fontScale or fontWeightAdjust. (2) The recreated activity starts a new React surface in the SAME JS runtime. Its ExpoRoot starts at the initial URL, which is '/' for a launcher intent. latestRootOnly (loop 7) only makes the old root render null; it does not bring back the route. The ranked game is not lost: gameStore (a module-level zustand store) still holds `online`, and the RemoteGameHost reconnects by itself (AppState goes background then active during the relaunch). But no screen shows it, and Home has no way back. (3) Nothing on Home checks for a live game. When the player taps Play ranked, startRanked calls detach(), then online.close(), then host.close(), then shutdown('left'), then room.leave(true). That is a CONSENTED leave, so the server makes it a hard disconnect at once and the 15 s grace runs. matchmaking.playing still holds the account until the room reports the end, so the new search is refused with alreadyQueued, and the game ends as an abandonment (a loss). If the player never searches, the opponent simply plays on alone, and the game is still lost (28 to 4.5 in the report). Loop 7 fixed a symptom of recreation (the dead navigation container). It never kept or restored the route, and it added nothing that sends the player back to a game the store still holds.
findings.evidence:
Manifest (prebuilt, regenerated by prebuild; android/ is gitignored, .gitignore:12): apps/mobile/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml MainActivity `android:configChanges="keyboard|keyboardHidden|orientation|screenSize|screenLayout|uiMode|smallestScreenSize|assetsPaths|locale|layoutDirection"`. No density, fontScale or fontWeightAdjust. The template's base value comes from node_modules/@expo/config-plugins/build/plugins/withAndroidBaseMods.js:79. expo-localization's plugin appends `|locale` and `|layoutDirection` (node_modules/expo-localization/plugin/src/withExpoLocalization.ts:79-84).
MainActivity.kt: `super.onCreate(null)`, so nothing is restored, and ReactDelegate.loadApp (node_modules/react-native/ReactAndroid/.../ReactDelegate.kt:322-329) creates a NEW surface with reactHost.createSurface. ReactDelegate.onHostDestroy (:164-175) calls unloadApp, which stops the old surface. The JS runtime and the ReactHost stay.
Store survives: apps/mobile/app/game.tsx:58-63 clears the store on unmount only when `leaving.current` is set, so recreation leaves `online` alive.
The host reconnects by itself: remoteGameHost.ts:1525-1540 (background: leave(false), then lose('background'); on 'active' it comes back with the token). AppStateModule.kt:41-48 emits background and active on the old activity's onHostPause and the new one's onHostResume.
Search kills the game: gameStore.ts:148-158 `detach = () => { ... online?.close(); ... }`, called from goRanked (gameStore.ts:230). onlineSession.ts:339-348 close() → host.close(). remoteGameHost.ts:612-613 close() → shutdown('left'), and :1574 `if (room) void room.leave(true)`. Server GameRoom.ts:530-531 `const consented = code === CloseCode.CONSENTED; this.game.disconnect(seat.playerId, { soft: !consented })` is the hard grace. matchmaking/service.ts:312-313 `if (this.playing.has(identity.userId)) throw new MatchmakingRefusal('alreadyQueued', 'this account is in a ranked game that has not ended')`. playing is set at GO (:844) and cleared only at the end (:972).
No route back: useAuthGate.ts:57-64 resumes only a remembered FRIENDS room (`roomToResume(owner)`) when path === ''. Nothing reads gameStore. Its `started` is a per-root useRef, so it runs again on every recreation.
Timeline, from Android's relaunch order (ActivityThread.handleRelaunchActivity: pause, stop and destroy the old activity, then create, start and resume the new one; typical totals 300-800 ms, estimated, no logcat of this run): t0 wm density; ~t0+50 old onPause gives AppState 'background', and the host does leave(false) (server onDrop: soft phase, the opponent sees nothing); ~+100 old onDestroy stops the old surface, and the old root unmounts with no clear(); ~+200-500 the new onCreate starts a new surface, latestRootOnly draws it (no older root still drawing), and ExpoRoot starts at '/' (Home); its useFocusEffect calls refreshHome; ~+300-800 the new onResume gives 'active', and the host reconnects with the token (server onReconnect; well under the 10 s soft phase). From then on the player is on Home while the server game runs. Later, Play ranked gives a consented leave plus alreadyQueued; 15 s later it is abandonment, the opponent wins, and the rating drops (−13).
findings.proposedFix: Two layers, both needed (see the next findings). (A) Stop recreation for density, fontScale and fontWeightAdjust with a small config plugin. (B) A resume path: when a root mounts with a live game in the store, it starts on /game (or /match or /friends/room); after a cold start or JS reload, it asks a local record or the server and goes back in. Also make Home's ranked, practice and friends starts refuse to silently consented-leave a live ranked or friends game. Send the player to /game instead.
findings.risks: None of this can be verified on the phone without a new APK (the manifest is native). (A) alone does not cover the other recreation causes. Those include bold text before fontWeightAdjust is listed, mcc/mnc, navigation/touchscreen, 'Don't keep activities', and the Android system killing the process in the background. They also include the in-app JS reload on a language change (languageSync.ts:72,93 restartApp → Updates.reloadAsync), which loses the store like a process kill.

findings.item: Angle A, option (a): android:configChanges for density|fontScale|fontWeightAdjust. Does RN 0.86 keep up in place?
findings.rootCause: RN 0.86 (bridgeless, Fabric, enableFontScaleChangesUpdatingLayout=true by default) handles density and fontScale changes in place when the activity is not recreated. The forwarding chain exists, and Expo's delegate wrapper passes it on. Loop 7 decided against it because react-native-svg reads the density once. That concern is only partly true: SVGs with a viewBox stay correct, and only SVGs without a viewBox (about 12 in the app) draw at the old scale until they remount. The Skia density is already stale after a recreation too, so this adds nothing new there. One more gap: JS fontScale updates only on onHostResume. A font change made in Settings (pause, then resume) reaches JS. `adb shell settings put system font_scale` with the app in the foreground reaches native text but not useWindowDimensions().fontScale, until the next background and foreground. Confidence is high for the forwarding and the fontScale relayout (read in source). It is medium-high that `wm density` relayouts every view in place: ViewRootImpl must remeasure ReactSurfaceView after the change even though the window's px size is the same. It normally does, and ReactHostImpl's requestLayout covers the fontScale case. This needs a device check.
findings.evidence:
Forwarding: ReactActivity.java:165-167 → ReactActivityDelegate.java:238-239 → ReactDelegate.kt:237-241 `reactHost?.onConfigurationChanged(activity)`. Expo's ReactActivityDelegateWrapper.kt:358-362 forwards it, after loadAppReady.
ReactHostImpl.kt:736-753: `if (ReactNativeFeatureFlags.enableFontScaleChangesUpdatingLayout()) { val previousFontScale = PixelUtil.toPixelFromSP(1.0); DisplayMetricsHolder.initDisplayMetrics(currentReactContext); ... if (previousFontScale != newFontScale) attachedSurfaces.forEach { it.view?.requestLayout() } }`, then AppearanceModule.onConfigurationChanged. The flag defaults to true (ReactNativeFeatureFlagsDefaults.kt:76).
Surface: ReactSurfaceView.onMeasure/onLayout (ReactSurfaceView.kt:110-127) → ReactSurfaceImpl.updateLayoutSpecs (:178-193), which passes `context.resources.displayMetrics.density` and `getFontScale(context)` (:219-221) to setLayoutConstraints.
C++: SurfaceHandler.cpp:321-327 `if (enableFontScaleChangesUpdatingLayout() && layoutContext.fontSizeMultiplier != old...) dirtyMeasurableNodes(*newRoot)`. YogaLayoutableShadowNode.cpp:476-507 reconfigures every child whose pointScaleFactor differs. LayoutMetrics.h:42,88 makes pointScaleFactor part of equality, so every node gets an UpdateLayout with the new density.
JS Dimensions: ReactRootView.java:940-947 onGlobalLayout → checkForDeviceDimensionsChanges → DeviceInfoModule.emitUpdateDimensionsEvent (DeviceInfoModule.kt:117-127). It emits 'didUpdateDimensions' when width, height, scale, densityDpi or fontScale differ, and density changes scale and densityDpi. The fontScale field updates only in onHostResume (~:100-106).
The app reads fontScale through useWindowDimensions (Board.tsx:66, ClockDigits.tsx:39, StarsBar.tsx:248, PlayerCardCompact.tsx:124, Rating.tsx:89, Button.tsx:158, ConfirmModal.tsx:138), so it follows the event.
SVG: node_modules/react-native-svg/android/.../SvgView.java:67 and VirtualView.java:39 `mScale = DisplayMetricsHolder.getScreenDisplayMetrics().density` (in the constructor). With a viewBox, SvgView.drawChildren (:305-321) maps vbRect (×mScale) to eRect (canvas px), so the old mScale cancels out. Without one, nothing maps it, and the drawing is off by newDensity/oldDensity. App <Svg> without a viewBox: TimerRing.tsx:91 (in game), GraceRing.tsx:45 (in game), HitBanner.tsx:165 (in game), StarCrown.tsx:98,164, ChapterGateway.tsx:175,224,305,327, MapRoad.tsx:170, MapScenery.tsx:112,130.
Skia: PlatformContext.java:32 takes the density once per ReactContext, which also survives a recreation, so this is not new.
findings.proposedFix: New config plugin apps/mobile/plugins/withActivityConfigChanges.js, modeled on expo-localization's: withAndroidManifest → AndroidConfig.Manifest.getMainActivityOrThrow. Append each missing token from ['density','fontScale','fontWeightAdjust'] to android:configChanges, idempotently. Add it to app.json `plugins` after expo-localization. app.json files are hashed by build-apk, so prebuild reruns. Add a unit test that runs the plugin's mod on a sample manifest (style of src/__tests__/appConfig.test.ts:547ff), including idempotency. Add viewBox={`0 0 ${w} ${h}`} to the 12 <Svg> listed (no visual change at the same density; correct after an in-place density change). As an alternative, key them by useWindowDimensions().scale. Optional: for `adb settings put system font_scale` with the app in the foreground, MainActivity.onConfigurationChanged (through the plugin's withMainActivity) could emit 'didUpdateDimensions' with DisplayMetricsHolder.getDisplayMetricsWritableMap(newConfig.fontScale). Otherwise QA should change the font through Settings, or background and foreground the app once. Keep latestRootOnly: other changes still recreate.

Skia canvases (ambient, interferences) keep the old density until the app restarts; this is the same as today. AvatarArt.tsx:492 memoizes PixelRatio.get() (pixel snapping only). StyleSheet.hairlineWidth is computed once. Minor, cosmetic, transient. The in-place relayout under `wm density` is the part with medium-high rather than full confidence.

findings.proposedFix:
Client:
(1) Recreation, JS alive: in app/+native-intent.tsx redirectSystemPath, when `initial`, return '/game' if useGameStore has a live game: `online` whose game is not over, a lobby or countdown, or a running practice `session`. Return '/match' if `match` is searching. Do this before roomLinkOf, but let an explicit room link still go to the InviteLinkPrompt flow (spec §6.6 table: 'אתה באמצע משחק… חזרה למשחק'). (2) Cold start or JS reload: a persisted record `activeRanked` {roomId, gameType, queueKey, matchId, profiles, owner, at}, through zustand persist/syncStorage like pendingInvite. findings.item: 1) density-change-orphans-ranked-game (MAJOR): what actually loses the game after an activity recreation
findings.rootCause: The game is NOT lost by the recreation itself. The JS runtime survives, and so do useGameStore.online (the live OnlineSession and RemoteGameHost) and the socket, which drops and reconnects through AppState. What breaks is that the new React root always opens on Home ('/'), and nothing in the app routes a fresh root back to a game that is still in memory. The only per-root start check in useAuthGate is for friends rooms. Home has no 'game in progress' entry. When the player then taps a ranked card, startRanked runs goRanked, which calls detach() and so online.close(). That shuts the host down with room.leave(true), a CONSENTED leave. The server treats a consented leave as a hard disconnect, so the 15 s grace starts at once. The new search is refused alreadyQueued because matchmaking.playing still holds the account until the game ends. Then the abandonment is recorded as a loss (-13). If the player never taps search, the session stays connected but idle, and the opponent plays on to a win. Either way the result is a loss. Loop 7 changed nothing here: latestRoot only decides which root draws. The old surface is stopped anyway by ReactDelegate.unloadApp(). Confidence: high that the store and the socket survive, that the new root is always '/', and that search calls detach() and a consented leave, which leads to alreadyQueued. Medium on which of the two endings caused this loss.
findings.evidence:
Millisecond timeline. The order of the Android and RN callbacks is from source; the times are typical, not measured on the phone.
- T0: `wm density 540`. The manifest has no `density` and no `fontScale`: apps/mobile/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:21 configChanges="keyboard|keyboardHidden|orientation|screenSize|screenLayout|uiMode|smallestScreenSize|assetsPaths|locale|layoutDirection". So ActivityThread relaunches MainActivity.
- T+~5 ms: onPause, then ReactHost.onHostPause, then AppState 'background'. RemoteGameHost.onAppState (remoteGameHost.ts:1511-1537) sets `backgrounded=true` and calls `room.leave(false)`. On the server, GameRoom.onDrop (GameRoom.ts:461-479) starts the soft phase and holds the seat (abandonmentAt + slack).
- T+~10 ms: onDestroy, then ReactDelegate.onHostDestroy, then unloadApp() and `reactSurface?.stop()` (node_modules/react-native/ReactAndroid/.../ReactDelegate.kt:164-172, 344-346). ReactHostImpl.onHostDestroy(activity) (runtime/ReactHostImpl.kt:314-323) only moves the lifecycle state. The instance and the JS runtime stay. The old root unmounts. app/game.tsx:57-62 clears the store only `if (leaving.current)`, so the session stays in useGameStore.
- T+~50-300 ms: MainActivity.onCreate calls `super.onCreate(null)` (no saved state) and loadApp('main'). A new React root starts: latestRootOnly gives it order 2. expo-router's initial URL is the root URL (getLinkingConfig.js:60-88), so the root shows Home. useAuthGate's start effect (src/auth/useAuthGate.ts:57-64) is per root (useRef) and only handles `roomToResume(owner)`, a friends room. There is nothing for ranked or practice.
- onResume: AppState 'active', then comeBack() and a reconnect with the token. GameRoom.onReconnect (GameRoom.ts:500-509) sends a snapshot. The game is live in useGameStore.online, and no screen shows it.
- T+N s: the player taps search. startRankedAndOpen (src/screens/home/startGame.ts:87) calls store.startRanked, then goRanked, then `detach()` (src/game/gameStore.ts:166-175: `match?.close(); online?.close()`). Then host.close() and shutdown('left'), which sends `room.leave(true)` (remoteGameHost.ts:1574). GameRoom.onLeave gets `consented = code === CloseCode.CONSENTED` and calls `game.disconnect(..., { soft: !consented })` (GameRoom.ts:530-531): hard at once.
- The same tick: the server's enqueue reaches `if (this.playing.has(identity.userId)) throw new MatchmakingRefusal('alreadyQueued', 'this account is in a ranked game that has not ended')` (apps/server/src/matchmaking/service.ts:312-313).
- T+N+15 s: abandonment, then the game is over and gameEnded() clears `playing` (service.ts:971-972). The loss is in the history.
Second victim of the same mechanism: a practice. Home's useFocusEffect runs refreshHome(), which does `if (session) { clear(); ... }` (HomeScreen.tsx:119-121, 325-330), so a recreation mid-practice saves the practice as interrupted. Child effects run before RootLayout's gate effect, so a router.push from useAuthGate would come too late for a practice.
Friends survive a recreation by luck: the new root's gate pushes /room/<code>?resume=1, and joinByCode returns the live session (`here.friendsCode === code && status !== 'closed'`, src/net/friends.ts:414-421).
findings.proposedFix:
Ranked by value.
(1) In-memory resume on every new root. This is the actual fix for item 1, and it needs no server change. Add `isRecreatedRoot()` to src/services/latestRoot.tsx (counted > 1). Route a recreated root straight into the live flow BEFORE Home mounts. Use app/+native-intent.tsx `redirectSystemPath({ path, initial: true })`: expo-router calls it for the root URL too (getLinkingConfig.js:76-82). When isRecreatedRoot() is true and there is no room/deep link, return '/game' if useGameStore holds a live `online` (status not closed, view not over) or a `session`, return '/match' for a live `match`, return '/friends/room' for a friends lobby, and otherwise keep the path. Home then never mounts, so refreshHome never clears a practice. Keep useAuthGate's per-root start as a fallback: if the store still holds a live online or match after settle, router.replace there. The same hook can later reopen /levels/play for a live stage.
(2) Never let a start action silently kill a live online game. In startRankedAndOpen, startAndOpen and the Home/modes entry points: if useGameStore.online is a ranked or friends game that is not over, router.push('/game') instead of startRanked (or ask first).
(3) The alreadyQueued screen offers 'Back to the game'. It is a new t() key in all 19 locales. It shows when the store holds the live game, or when the server endpoint from item 2 returns one. Then go through the resume path of item 2.
(4) Do NOT add density to configChanges (see the next finding).
Tests (Jest): extend src/services/__tests__/latestRoot.test.tsx, which goes through index.ts and two roots. A fake-server ranked game is live in root 1. Root 2 mounts. Check that its initial route is /game with the same online.key, that host.close and leave(true) are never called (spy), and that no 'game' FlowFallback shows. The same with a practice session: it is not cleared or interrupted. And with a live search: root 2 is on /match. A unit test: startRankedAndOpen with a live ranked online goes to /game and does not call detach.
findings.risks: Low risk in the redirect hook: it only acts when counted > 1 (never on a cold start) and only when the store holds a live flow. Check the case where an Android task was launched by a room link: the recreated activity's intent still has the link, and redirectSystemPath must still handle that first, as today. If /game is the only route in the stack, dismissTo('/') replaces it with Home, which works; unstable_settings.initialRouteName='index' would put Home under it. It needs a new APK. The phone check: mid ranked 2P, run wm density 540 and then wm density reset. The app comes back on the board, the opponent sees at most a short soft-offline dot, and the game finishes normally. Another agent could still add a new path that calls startRanked or detach while a game is live; fix (2) covers the known ones.

findings.item: Option (a), android:configChanges for density/fontScale: why it cannot replace a resume path (RN 0.86.3 source)
findings.rootCause: With configChanges, React Native 0.86 bridgeless does part of the in-place work for a density change, but not all of it. ReactHostImpl.onConfigurationChanged re-reads DisplayMetricsHolder and calls requestLayout on the surfaces only when the FONT SCALE changed. It never sends `didUpdateDimensions` to JS. Only the old-architecture ReactRootView and DeviceInfoModule.onHostResume send it, and the latter only for a fontScale change. So JS Dimensions, PixelRatio and useWindowDimensions would stay on the old density: 33 app files read them. Native views that cache the density would also draw at the old scale until they are created again. react-native-svg is one, and it draws the app's icons and avatars. Recreation also comes from changes configChanges cannot cover (bold text/fontWeightAdjustment, and others), from 'Don't keep activities', and from the process being killed in the background. So a resume path is needed anyway. Confidence: high for the source facts, medium for how much would look wrong on the phone (needs a device check).
findings.evidence:
- ReactActivity.java:165-167 forwards onConfigurationChanged to the delegate. Expo's ReactActivityDelegateWrapper.kt:358-362 forwards it after loadAppReady. ReactDelegate.kt:237-241 calls `reactHost?.onConfigurationChanged(activity)`.
- runtime/ReactHostImpl.kt:736-754: `if (enableFontScaleChangesUpdatingLayout()) { ...; DisplayMetricsHolder.initDisplayMetrics(currentReactContext); if (previousFontScale != newFontScale) attachedSurfaces.forEach { it.view?.requestLayout() } }`, then only AppearanceModule. No dimensions event.
- modules/deviceinfo/DeviceInfoModule.kt:105-111: onHostResume sends emitUpdateDimensionsEvent only `if (newFontScale != fontScale)`. A search for callers of emitUpdateDimensionsEvent finds only that one and ReactRootView.java:1016/1062 (old architecture).
- fabric/FabricUIManagerBinding.kt:115: `setPixelDensity(getDisplayMetricDensity())` runs once at register. The surface's layout constraints do take the density again on each measure (runtime/ReactSurfaceImpl.kt:184-191).
- react-native-svg: VirtualView.java:39 and SvgView.java:67 set `mScale = DisplayMetricsHolder.getScreenDisplayMetrics().density` in the constructor.
- Side note, lower confidence: on the recreation path, nothing in bridgeless calls DisplayMetricsHolder.initDisplayMetrics again. The only callers are ReactRootView.java:140/1010 and ReactHostImpl.kt:741, and getDisplayMetricDensity reads the copied screen metrics. So after a density change with the app open, RN's screen density and the JS Dimensions may stay stale until the process restarts, even with recreation. This may affect the QA's 360dp/density-480 runs that set the density with the app open.
findings.proposedFix: Keep the manifest as it is for density. Optional and separate: a config plugin (with a test on its output) that adds only `fontScale` to configChanges. The native relayout is handled, but JS fontScale only updates at the next onHostResume, which always happens when the change is made in the Settings app and never with adb while the app is in front. If it is done, add a JS-side refresh (for example, on AppState 'active' compare PixelRatio.getFontScale() with the last value). The fix for item 1 is the resume path.
findings.risks: Adding density would give wrong sizes for the SVG avatars and icons, and a stale useWindowDimensions (the board size), until a restart. That is worse than a clean recreation. Even fontScale in place leaves JS stale in the adb case, and it needs a device check.

findings.item: 2) Cold-start (process killed) resume for ranked: where state lives, what the server knows, and the API/flow
findings.rootCause: The client keeps nothing of a ranked game outside JS memory. The gameStore comment says it: 'not persisted: ... a ranked one on the server' (src/game/gameStore.ts:45). The reservation is good only once, and the roomId and the reconnection token die with the process. Friends rooms have a persisted record and a start-up resume: auth/pendingInvite.ts `room` in the expo-sqlite kv-store, written by followCurrentRoom (InviteLinkPrompt.tsx:244-266) and read by useAuthGate (roomToResume). Ranked has neither. The server side is ready since loop 8. A match room's roomId is its 6-character code. GameRoom.onJoin lets the same identity back into its seat when the seat is held for a dropped connection (takeover), or when it was left on purpose (sessionId null), until abandonment. maxClients is doubled for match rooms. But the server has no way to TELL an app which room it is in. matchmaking.playing maps userId to a matchId only, set at GO and cleared at gameEnded. The Match object, with its roomId, is deleted from `matches` at GO.
findings.evidence:
- Server: GameRoom.ts:428-453 (onJoin: seat of identity; `heldSeats.get(seat.sessionId)` takeover, otherwise alreadyInRoom while still open); GameRoom.ts:403 `this.maxClients = (setup.playerCount - bots.length) * (this.match ? 2 : 1)`; GameRoom.ts:384-393 (the roomId is the code: roomIdIsCode() returns true); GameRoom.ts:515-532 (after a consented leave the seat is null, so it can be taken back within the grace); spec 16.2 allows a return 'by the reconnection token or by the room code'.
- matchmaking/service.ts:271-272 `private readonly playing = new Map<string, string>()` (user to match id); :840-845 go(): `this.matches.delete(match.id); for (m) this.playing.set(m.userId, match.id)` and `session.send({ type: 'started', matchId, roomId })`; :428-430 isPlaying(); :971-972 gameEnded().
- Client: the rejoin by id already exists. OnlineRequest `{ kind: 'join', code, gameType }`, then host.join(code), then client.joinById(code, whoAmI()) (onlineSession.ts:219-222, onlineClient.ts:173-177). retryOnline already uses it for a match (`online.host.roomCode`, which is room.roomId: remoteGameHost.ts:785; gameStore.ts:297-303). protocol MatchSeatReservation has `roomId` (packages/protocol/src/matchmaking.ts:187-194), so the room is known from 'found', before GO.
- Missing: a retry for alreadyInRoom on the 'join' path. Only enterFriends retries (remoteGameHost.ts:497-515, friendsHeldSeatDelaysMs).
- Friends cold start: useAuthGate.ts:57-64 runs roomToResume, then /room/<code>?resume=1, then joinByCode(code,'resume'), then POST /v1/rooms/join, then takeFriendsSeat. Loop 8 says this works against the new server, so friends needs no change for a process kill.
findings.proposedFix:
The flow, in order of preference.
(A) The server is the source of truth, with a new authenticated route, for example GET /v1/me/game (keep it out of /v1/me: the accounts router has no matchmaking). In MatchmakingService, keep `{ matchId, roomId, queueKey }` per user. Fill it once the room is opened (match.roomId is set at :753), so a kill during the VS or countdown is covered too, and keep it until gameEnded or closed. Expose activeGameOf(userId). The route returns `{ game: { kind: 'ranked', roomId, queueKey, gameType, players } | null }`, and optionally the friends room from FriendRoomsService. Rate-limit it like the other reads. An older app never calls it, and a newer app treats 404 from an older server as 'unknown' and falls back to (B).
(B) A local record, mirroring pendingInvite's `room`. A small persisted store, for example src/game/currentGame.ts: `{ roomId, queueKey, owner uid, at, profiles(name, avatarId, country, rating) }`. Written when a match session gets its reservation ('found') and refreshed when AppState is not active. Forgotten when the session sees `over` (spec 16.2: the app does not reconnect to a game whose end it saw), on leaving on purpose (gameStore.clear or detach), on a refusal for good, and after a TTL of about 2 min (abandonment at 25 s, plus the 60 s closeAfterGameMs to still see the results).
(C) Resume at start, in useAuthGate's per-root start effect (Home only, signed in, same owner). Ask (A), falling back to (B). If there is a game: `useGameStore.getState().startOnline({ kind: 'join', code: roomId, gameType }, deviceHost, profiles)`, then router.push('/game'). The existing OnlineGame connecting and reconnect screens show it. The friends branch stays as it is. Add to host.join the same alreadyInRoom retry as enterFriends, until graceEndsAt or about 25 s, for a half-open socket. If the room is gone or refuses for good (notFound, gameStarted, over and closed), forget the record and stay on Home, with at most a toast.
(D) Item 1's alreadyQueued screen uses the same resume.
Tests. Server: activeGameOf is set when the room opens and at GO, and cleared at over, closed or cancelled; the route returns 401 signed out and null when idle; contract test: a joinById after a dropped or a consented leave within the grace gets the seat and a snapshot (extend gameRoom.ranked.test.ts and appMatchmaking.contract.test.ts); old-client compatibility, where alreadyQueued is unchanged. Client: currentGame is saved at found and forgotten at over and on clear; a cold start with a saved record and a fake server with a held seat opens /game on the same room; an alreadyInRoom refusal retries; a refusal for good forgets the record and stays on Home; a record of another uid is ignored.
findings.risks: The matchmaking state is in memory. After a server restart the room is gone too, and the route returns null, which is correct. If several server instances ever run, the route must ask the instance that holds the room. A stale local record must never re-enter a game the player saw end, so forget it at 'over'. One small authenticated GET on each cold start, and only when signed in and on Home. The edits touch shared files (useAuthGate, gameStore, startGame) that other agents edit: keep them small. New strings ('Back to the game', a 'Rejoining your game' toast if one is used) need all 19 locales. It needs a server deploy plus a new APK to check on a phone: kill the app mid ranked game, reopen within about 15 s, and it should land on the same board.

items.rootCause: Three links in a chain, all checked in source. (1) `wm density`, Display size, Font size and bold text recreate MainActivity. The manifest's configChanges do not list density, fontScale or fontWeightAdjust. (2) The new React root runs in the same JS runtime. The game store (a module) still holds the live ranked OnlineSession, and its RemoteGameHost reconnects by itself: AppState goes background then active, then leave(false) and a reconnect inside the soft phase. But the new root's ExpoRoot starts at the launcher URL '/'. latestRootOnly (loop 7) only decides which root draws. Nothing sent a new root back to the game the store held, and Home had no way into it. (3) On Home, "Play" runs startRanked, then goRanked, then detach(), then online.close(), then host.close(), then room.leave(true). That is a CONSENTED leave, which the server makes hard at once: the grace runs, then abandonment, a loss. matchmaking.playing still held the account, so the search was refused alreadyQueued, and the refusal did not say which game. If the player never searched, the game simply ran on without them, and that also ended as a loss.
items.fix: Fixed in the app, with no native change. (A) A new game/liveFlow.ts reads what the store still holds. app/+native-intent.tsx redirectSystemPath, when `initial` is true and something is under way, starts the new root on its screen instead of Home or the replayed link: /game for an online game or a practice, /match for a search or a VS, /friends/room for a friends lobby. A first start always has an empty store, so this never fires then. As a fallback, useAuthGate's start on Home calls resumeAtStart, which does the same. (B) startAndOpen and startRankedAndOpen (screens/home/startGame.ts) open the live online game instead of starting something new. So Home, the game-type screen and the bot screen can never consented-leave a running ranked or friends game. (C) Server: `matchmaking.playing` keeps the room id, and the alreadyQueued refusal for a running ranked game now says `... (room <id>)` (protocol rankedGameRefusalText and matchmakingRoomOf). An older app reads only the prefix, so nothing changes for it. On the match error screen, alreadyQueued with a room shows "Back to the game" (match:error.backToGame, 19 locales, the same wording as friends busy.game.back) in place of "Search again". It rejoins that room by id with the same account and pushes /game over the match screen. android:configChanges was NOT changed. In RN 0.86, density in place re-reads DisplayMetricsHolder and emits didUpdateDimensions on the next global layout. But react-native-svg's SvgView and VirtualView cache the density in their constructors, so SVGs without a viewBox draw at the old scale; Skia keeps its density; and fontScale in place does not reach JS when changed by adb with the app in front (DeviceInfoModule updates fontScale only onHostResume). Recreation also comes from changes configChanges cannot list, so the app must survive it anyway. With this fix it does.

items.deviceCheck: Needs a SERVER DEPLOY (loop 8 + this round) and a NEW APK (JS). Phone 3, English, signed in, staging. 1) Start a ranked 2P fast game. When the board shows, place a digit, then run `adb shell wm density 540`. Expect: within about 1 s the app is back on the SAME board, not Home. The timer goes on and my digits are there. The opponent's phone shows no 'opponent disconnecting' banner (soft phase). Place another digit: it is accepted. 2) Run `adb shell wm density reset`, then `adb shell settings put system font_scale 1.3`, then `font_scale 1.0`. Each time it is the same board. Play to the end: the result is a normal win or loss, not abandonment, and the history shows that result. 3) During a search ('Searching…'), run `wm density 540`: the app stays on the search screen; then `wm density reset`. 4) A friends room, in the GAME phase: run `wm density 540`. items.rootCause: After a process kill or JS reload, the app kept nothing of a ranked game. The room id and the reconnection token lived only in JS memory (gameStore says 'not persisted'). The start (useAuthGate) resumed only a remembered FRIENDS room. The server has accepted the same account back into its held seat by room id since loop 8 (GameRoom holdSeat + takeover, match maxClients ×2), but the app never asked for it. So the player landed on Home and the game ended as abandonment. Friends after a kill already worked: roomToResume, then /room/<code>?resume=1, then POST /v1/rooms/join. Friends after a recreation now goes through item 1's redirect.
items.fix: New apps/mobile/src/game/rankedResume.ts. followRankedGame (started once per root in useAuthGate) keeps 'the ranked game I am in' in expo-sqlite kv ('ranked-game'): {roomId, gameType, owner uid, at, players' public cards}, never a token. It is written once the match room is joined, its time refreshed when the app leaves the foreground, and forgotten when the store lets go of the game (a deliberate leave or a surrender), when the end is seen, or when the connection is given up. At the start on Home, signed in and with no friends room to resume, resumeAtStart(owner) acts. If the store still holds something (a recreation), it opens that screen. Otherwise, if a record exists for this owner and is under 2 h old, it quietly joins the room again by id with the same account (store.startOnline({kind:'join'}, deviceHost, profiles); startOnline now accepts profiles) and pushes /game once the room takes it. On alreadyInRoom or network it tries again after 2, 4, 8 and 12 s. Any other refusal (notFound, gone, over) forgets the record and clears the store, and Home stays, with no error screen at start. A late return while the finished room is still open shows the end, then the record is forgotten. Compatibility: no protocol message changed. An older server without loop 8 refuses the join, so Home stays.

rep.notes:
Design decision: I fixed the real cause, the missing way back into a live game, and did NOT stop activity recreation. Option (a), adding density/fontScale/fontWeightAdjust to configChanges, was checked in the RN 0.86 source. It mostly works in place: ReactHostImpl.onConfigurationChanged re-reads DisplayMetricsHolder, and ReactSurfaceView (a ReactRootView) emits didUpdateDimensions on the next global layout. But react-native-svg caches the density in the SvgView and VirtualView constructors, so the 12 SVGs without a viewBox (TimerRing, GraceRing, HitBanner, StarCrown, the map) would draw at the wrong scale. Skia keeps its density. And a fontScale changed by adb with the app in front does not reach JS until a resume. That cannot be verified without a native build, which is not allowed now, and recreation also comes from bold text and other changes. This is the same conclusion loop 7 reached. If Moshe wants fewer recreations later: a config plugin plus viewBox on those 12 SVGs, then a device pass.

Residual, not fixed: in a friends room's LOBBY (before the game), a recreation still leaves the room. The old root's /friends/room unmount cleanup calls friendsRooms().leave(), because Android stops the old surface before the new root mounts. Nothing is lost before a game, but the seat goes. The friends GAME phase is fine. A fix would need a reliable 'root is being torn down' signal in that cleanup.

The 'Back to the game' button on alreadyQueued appears only with the new server: the room id now comes in the refusal text. Against an older server the cold-start local record still resumes. I did not add GET /v1/me/game; the refusal text plus the local record cover the cases. widthBudget.test.ts fails because of Toast.tsx, which another agent is editing; it is unrelated to these changes. No adb, no build, no deploy, no git operations.
